label: verify-t2-patterns-law

claims.claim: Law set 1.8.1 has no accepted law about spatial patterns or fronts; only relevant pins are candidates fisher-kpp-speed and turing-ddi; turing-wavelength is not pinned.
claims.source_says: lawset-1.8.1.json: fisher-kpp-speed status candidate v1.1.0; turing-ddi status candidate v1.1.0; no turing-wavelength entry. Theorems kpp_min_speed and turing_instability match. turing-wavelength.json: "introduced_in": null
claims.note: Pins and theorem names reproduce; the accepted list (Kimura, Fisher FTNS, scaling, Laplace, etc.) contains no front or pattern law, though 'none' rests on reading ids only.

claims.claim: The older map's Turing.lean/CellGeometry.lean laws are absent from the application repo at 1.8.1 (exist only in upstream/leanbio 1.6.0).
claims.source_says: App lean/Delphi lists Altitude...Thompson, no Turing.lean or CellGeometry.lean. upstream/leanbio/lean/Delphi lists CellGeometry.lean, Crystals.lean, Turing.lean.
claims.note: Directory listings match; the '1.6.0' label of the upstream copy was only loosely checked.

claims.claim: NarlaSpeed.lean passes check.sh with no errors and no sorryAx, axioms only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound; the sorry mutant fails.
claims.source_says: check_ok.txt: errors=0 sorryAx=0 axiom-lines=10/10, ALL CHECKED, exit_ok=0. check_mutant.txt: sorryAx=5 ... FAILED, exit_mutant=1
claims.note: Output files confirm it; I did not re-run Lean, as instructed.

claims.claim: Narla et al. report a square-root dependence of front speed on growth rate, which the new Lean law formalises (exponent 1/2 at fixed X, Da, A).
claims.source_says: First, there is a square root dependence on the growth rate r, as validated by numerical results in Fig. 2A.
claims.note: Sentence found in PMC8640786 full text; the fixed X, Da, A condition and the Lean statement were not checked against the paper.

overall: All four key claims reproduce from the registry files, directory listings, check outputs and the Europe PMC full text. Caveat: the Narla quote was not tied to the specific closed form used in the Lean file.
